Urania.definition: Ūrania ae (C.), or Ūraniē, ēs (O.), f , *ou)rani/a, the Muse of Astronomy, Urania.

Urios.definition: Urios (-us) ī, m a title of Jupiter.

ubertas.definition: ūbertās ātis, f 2 uber, richness, fulness , plenteousness, plenty, abundance, copiousness, fruitfulness, fertility, productiveness : mammarum: in percipiendis fructibus: Rami bacarum ubertate incurvescere.—Fig., of mi…

ubertim.definition: ūbertim adv. 2 uber, abundantly, copiously : lacrimas fundere, Ct.

ubi.definition: ubi or ubī adv. old cubi for quo-bi, locat. from 1 qui.—Relat., in which place, in what place, where : tum eos agros, ubi hodie est haec urbs, incolebant: in ipso aditu atque ore portū s, ubi, etc.: ibi futuros Helvet…

ubicumque.definition: ubi-cumque or ubī-cumque (-cunque, old -quomque) adv. —Relat., wherever, wheresoever: etsi, ubicumque es, in eādem es navi: ego uni Ser vor, ubīcumque est, O.: Sis licet felix, ubicumque mavis, H.: ubicumque terrarum …

ubivis.definition: ubivīs adv. ubi+2d pers. sing. of volo, where you will, be it where it may, wherever it may be, anywhere, everywhere : nemo sit, quin ubivis, quam ibi, ubi est, esse malit: recito Non ubivis coramve quibuslibet, H.: u…

udus.definition: ūdus adj. for ūvidus, wet, moist, damp, humid : paludes, O.: litus, H.: pomaria rivis, H.: oculi, O.: Vere madent udo terrae, V.: udae Vocis iter (i. e. udum iter vocis), the throat , V.: liber, sappy , V.: argilla, y…

ulcero.definition: ulcerō —, ātus, āre ulcus, to make sore, cause to ulcerate : nondum ulcerato serpentis morsu: alcui lumbos onere, H.—Fig.: Non ancilla tuum iecur ulceret ulla, i. e. wound your heart , H.

ulcerosus.definition: ulcerōsus adj. ulcus, full of sores, ulcerous : facies, Ta.—Fig.: iecur, i. e. sore heart , H.

ulciscor.definition: ulcīscor ūltus, ī, dep., to avenge oneself on, take vengeance on, punish, recompense: ulciscendi Romanos, pro iis iniuriis, occasio, Cs.: (hominem) utinam ulcisci possem! sed illum ulciscentur mores sui: victor acerbi…

ulcus.definition: ulcus eris, n cf. e(/lkos, a sore, ulcer : ulceris os, V.: pudor malus ulcera celat, H.—Fig.: hoc ulcus tangere, i. e. this painful subject , T.: quicquid horum attigeris, ulcus est, i. e. it cannot bear examination .

uligo.definition: ūlīgō inis, f VG-, moisture, dampness : humus dulci uligine laeta, V.: profunda, Ta.

ullus.definition: ūllus gen. ūllīus (rarely ūllius, Ct., O.), dat. ūllī, adj. for * ūnulus, dim. of unus.—With a negation, expressed or implied, any, any one : nec tuos ludos aspexit, nec ullos alios: neque aliud ullum (signum), praete…

ulmeus.definition: ulmeus adj. ulmus, of elm-wood, of elm : cena, Iu.

ulmus.definition: ulmus ī, f 1 OL-, an elm, elm-tree : fecundae frondibus ulmi, V., H., O.: Falernae, i. e. on which the Falernian vines were trained , Iu.: viduae, without vines , Iu.

ulna.definition: ūlna ae, f cf. w)le/nh, the elbow : corpus ulnis attollo, O.: Eurydicen amplectitur ulnis, i. e. arms , O.—As a measure of length, an ell : Trīs spatium non amplius ulnas, V., H., O.

ultimus.definition: ūltimus (ūltumus) adj. sup. cf. ulterior.— In space, farthest, most distant, most remote, uttermost, extreme, last : (luna) quae ultima a caelo lucebat: in ultimam provinciam se coniecit, the most remote part of the p…

ultio.definition: ūltiō ōnis, f cf. ulciscor, a taking vengeance, avenging, revenge : quamquam serum auxilium perditis erat, tamen ultionem petens, L.: infirmi est animi voluptas Ultio, Iu.: prima est haec ultio, i. e. punishment , Iu.…

ultor.definition: ūltor ōris, f cf. ulciscor, a punisher, avenger, revenger : coniurationis ultor: Exoriare aliquis nostris ex ossibus ultor, V.: deus ultor, i. e. Anteros, O.—As a surname of Mars, the Avenger , O.

ultrix.definition: ultrīx īcis, adj. ultor, avenging, vengeful : ultrices Dirae, V.: Curae, V.

ulula.definition: ulula ae, f VL-, a screech-owl , V.

ululatus.definition: (ululātus, ūs) m ululo, a howling, wailing, shrieking, loud lamentation (only acc. and abl, sing . and plur.): subitis ululatibus Inplevere nemus, O.: ululatūs ore dedere, V.: lugubri et barbaro ululatu, Cu.: ululatum…

ululo.definition: ululō āvī, ātus, āre VL-, to howl, yell, shriek, wail, lament loudly : canes, V.: summoque ulularunt vertice Nymphae, V.: Canidia ululans, H.: Tisiphone thalamis ululavit in illis, O.: ululanti voce canere.— Poet.: pl…

ulva.definition: ulva ae, f 1 OL-, swamp-grass, sedge : palustris, V.: (aper) ulvis et harundine pinguis, H., O.

umbella.definition: umbella ae, f dim. umbra, a sunshade, parasol, umbrella , Iu.

umbilicus.definition: umbilīcus ī, m * umbalus (o)mfolo/s), the navel : ut umbilico tenus aqua esset, L.— The middle, centre : qui locus umbilicus Siciliae nominatur: terrarum, i. e. Delphi : orbis terrarum, L.: umbilicum Graeciae incolere…

umbo.definition: umbō ōnis, m AMB-, a swelling, rounded elevation, knob, boss : clipei, V.: umbonibus incussāque alā sternuntur hostes, L.: alā et umbone pulsantes, L.— A shield : nec sufficit umbo Ictibus, V.: iunctae umbone phalange…

umbra.definition: umbra ae, f a shade, shadow: terrae: colles . . . adferunt umbram vallibus: noctis se condidit umbris, V.: pampineae, of vines, V.: Falce premes umbram, i. e. prune the foliage, V.—Prov.: qui umbras timet, is afraid o…

umbraculum.definition: umbrāculum ī, n umbra, a shady place, bower, arbor : lentae texunt umbracula vites, V.: ex umbraculis eruditorum in solem, the retirement. —Plur., a sunshade, parasol : pellebant umbracula soles, O.

umbratilis.definition: umbrātilis e, adj. umbra, in the shade, in retirement, private, retired, contemplative : vita.— Of speech, in the manner of the schools, scholastic, esoteric : exercitatio: oratio philosophorum.

umbrifer.definition: umbrifer era, erum, adj. umbra+1 FER-, shade-bringing, casting shade, shady : platanus, C. poët.: nemus, V.

umbrosus.definition: umbrōsus adj. with comp. umbra, full of shade, rich in shade, shady, umbrageous : locus umbrosior: Heliconis orae, H.: Ida, O.: vallis, V.— Giving shade, casting shadows, shading : inter densas, umbrosa cacumina, fago…

umeo.definition: ūmeō (not hū-), —, —, ēre VG-, to be moist, be damp, be wet : calidā qui locus umet aquā, O.: Ument genae, O.— P. praes. : umens tellus, O.: oculi, suffused , O.: umbra, i. e. the cool night , V.— Plur n . as subst: F…

umerus.definition: umerus (not hum-), ī, m cf. w)=mos, the upper arm, shoulder : Exerit haec umerum, O.: sagittae pendebant ab umero: umerum apertum gladio appetit, Cs.: Pars umeri ima tui, O.: Demissis umeris esse, T.: umeri ad sustine…

umidulus.definition: ūmidulus adj. dim. umidus, rather damp, moist : linum, O.

umidus.definition: ūmidus (not hū-), adj. VG-, moist, humid, damp, dank, wet : natura animantis, vel terrena sit vel ignea vel umida: (naves) factae ex umidā materiā, Cs.: creta, H.: dies umida nimbis, O.: regna, i. e. of the river , V.…

umifer.definition: ūmifer (not hū-), fera, ferum, adj. VG-, 1 FER-, containing moisture, moist : sucus.

umor.definition: ūmor (not hū-), ōris, m VG-, a liquid, fluid, moisture : frigoribus durescit umor: umor adlapsus extrinsecus sudorem videtur imitari: circumfluus, the ocean , O.: lacteus, milk , O.: Bacchi Massicus, wine , V.: umor e…

umquam.definition: umquam or (later) unquam, adv.—Of time quom(cum)+quam, at any time, ever (opp. numquam; usu. with a negat . expressed or implied): quod (principium) si numquam oritur, ne occidit quidem umquam: cum ita sim adflictus u…

unanimitas.definition: ūnanimitās ātis, f unanimus, unanimity, concord : fraterna, L.

unanimus.definition: ūnanimus adj. unus+animus, of one mind, of one accord, in union, concordant : unanimam adloquitur sororem, V.: vos unanimi densate catervas, V.

uncia.definition: uncia ae, f cf. ūnus, ūnicus, the twelfth part, a twelfth : Caesar ex unicā, sed Lepta ex triente, heir to one twelfth.— A trifle, bit, atom : nulla uncia nobis Est eboris, Iu.

unciarius.definition: unciārius adj. uncia, of a twelfth part, containing a twelfth : faenus, at one twelfth of the principal yearly , i. e. 8 1/3 per cent ., L.

unciatim.definition: unciātim adv. uncia, by twelfths, by ounces ; hence, little by little : Quod ille unciatim vix de demenso suo . . . compersit miser, T.

uncinatus.definition: uncīnātus adj. uncīnus, a hook; from 1. uncus, barbed, hooked : corpora.

unciola.definition: unciola ae, f dim. uncia, a paltry twelfth , Iu.

unctio.definition: ūnctiō ōnis, f ungo, a besmearing, anointing : philosophum omnes unctionis causā relinquunt, i. e. to anoint themselves (for wrestling).

unctor.definition: ūnctor ōris, m ungo, an anointer .

unctus.definition: ūnctus adj. with comp. P. of ungo, anointed, oiled : nudus, unctus est contionatus: puer unctis Tractavit calicem manibus, i. e. greasy , H.—Fig., rich, luxurious, sumptuous : patrimonia, Ct.: melius et unctius, H.: i…

unda.definition: unda ae, f VD-, a wave, billow : spectaculum undis ipsis et litoribus luctuosum: Acherontis undae, V.: ponto Unda recumbit, H.: spumosae, O.—Sing collect. : prora remissa subito navem undae adfligebat, L.—Poet., of wr…

unde.definition: unde adv. for * cunde; 2 CA-. I. Of place. — Relat., from which place, whence : nec enim inde venit, unde mallem: ut eo restituerentur (Galli), unde deiecti essent: eodem, unde erant profectae (naves), Cs.: loca super…

undecim.definition: ūndecim or XI num. unus+decem, eleven : XI legiones: milia talentum.

undecimus.definition: ūndecimus adj. num. unus+decimus, the eleventh : hora: legio, L.: annus, V.

undenonaginta.definition: ūndēnōnāgintā num. unus+de+nonaginta, eighty-nine : naves, L.

undeoctoginta.definition: ūndeoctōgintā or LXXVIIII num. unus +de+octoginta, seventy-nine : unde-octoginta annos natus, H.: argenti bigati LXXVIIII, L.

undequinquagesimus.definition: ūndēquīnquāgēsimus (-gēnsimus) num adj. undequinquaginta, the forty-ninth : dies.

undequinquaginta.definition: ūndēquīnquāgintā num. unus+de+quinquaginta, forty-nine : coronae aureae, L.

undesexaginta.definition: ūndēsexāgintā num. unus+de+sexaginta, fifty-nine : vivi capti, L.

undevicesimus.definition: ūndēvīcēsimus (-cēnsimus) adj. undeviginti, the nineteenth : anno undevicesimo.

undeviginti.definition: ūndēvīgintī num. unus+de+viginti, nineteen : anni: signa militaria, L.

undique.definition: undique adv. unde+que, from all parts, from every quarter, on all sides, all around, on every part, everywhere : ut undique in hostīs impetus fieret, Cs.: rebus undique collectis: concurritur undique ad istum Syracusa…

undisonus.definition: undisonus adj. unda+SON-, wave-sounding : dei, i. e. sea-gods , Pr.

undo.definition: undō —, —, āre unda, to rise in waves, throw up waves, surge, swell : undanti in freto: Ad caelum undabat vortex, V.— To wave, undulate : undans fornacibus Aetna, V.: undantes habenae, flowing , V.

undosus.definition: undōsus adj. unda, full of waves, surging, billowy : dei, sea-gods , Pr. (al. undisonus).

unetvicesimani.definition: ūnetvīcēsimānī ōrum, m unetvicesimus, soldiers of the twenty-first legion , Ta.

unetvicesimus.definition: ūnetvīcēsimus num adj. unus+et+vicesimus, the twenty-first : legio, Ta.

ungo.definition: ungō or unguō unxī, ūnctus, ere, to smear, besmear, anoint: unctus est, accubuit: Arsuros artūs, O.: ter uncti Transnanto Tiberim, H.: caules oleo, dress with oil, H.: tela manu, to smear with poison, V.: arma uncta c…

unguentarius.definition: unguentārius ī, m unguentum, a dealer in unguents, perfumer , C., H.

unguentum.definition: unguentum ī, n unguo, an ointment, unguent, perfume : os unguento confricare: Huc vina et unguenta ferre, H.

unguiculus.definition: unguiculus ī, m dim. unguis, a finger-nail : a teneris unguiculis, from infancy .

unguis.definition: unguis is, abl. ungue (unguī, Ct., H.), m cf. o)/nuc.— On the finger or toe, a nail : acutus, H.: proprios purgans unguīs, H.: ab imis unguibus usque ad verticem summum, i. e. from head to foot : a rectā conscientiā t…

ungula.definition: ungula ae, f unguis, a hoof, claw, talon : vestigium ungulae: sonitu quatit ungula campum, V.—Prov.: toto corpore atque omnibus ungulis, i. e. with tooth and nail .—Poet.: cum carceribus missos rapit ungula currūs, i.…

unicus.definition: ūnicus adj. unus, only, sole, single, singular, unique : gnatus, T.: filius: filia, T.: consul, L.: maritus, H.: anser erat, O.— Alone of its kind, singular, uncommon, unparalleled, unique : aut summa neglegentia aut …

uniformis.definition: ūnifōrmis e, adj. unus+forma, having only one shape, uniform : quiddam, Ta.

unigena.definition: ūnigena ae, adj. unus+GEN-, only-begotten, only : mundus.— As subst m . and f a brother, sister , Ct.

unimanus.definition: ūnimanus adj. unus+manus, with a single hand, one-handed : puer natus, L.

universitas.definition: ūniversitās ātis, f universus, the whole, aggregate, entirety : generis humani, the whole human race : rerum, i. e. the universe.—The whole world, universe : in currum universitatis inponere.

universus.definition: ūniversus adj. unus+versus, all together, all in one, whole, entire, collective (opp. singuli): provincia: civitas: mundus: triduum, three days together , T.: de universis generibus rerum dicere: ut eadem sit utilitas…

urbanitas.definition: urbānitās ātis, f urbanus, a living in the city, city life, life in Rome : desideria urbis et urbanitatis.— City fashion, city manners, refinement, elegance, politeness, courtesy, affability, urbanity : addo urbanitat…

urbanus.definition: urbānus adj. with comp. and sup. urbs, of the city, of the town, in the city, in Rome : vitam urbanam atque otium Secutus sum, T.: tribus: praetor, Cs.: exercitus, L.: administratio rei p.— As subst n., an inhabitant …

urbs.definition: urbs urbis, f a walled town, city : Interea Aeneas urbem designat aratro, V.: Certabant urbem Romam Remoramne vocarent, Enn. ap. C.: urbes magnae atque imperiosae: duabus urbibus eversis: Romana (i. e. Roma), L.—Poet.…

urceolus.definition: urceolus ī, m dim. urceus, a little pitcher, small water-pot : urceoli sex, Iu.

urceus.definition: urceus ī, m a pitcher, water-pot, ewer, H.

uredo.definition: ūrēdō inis, f 1 VAS-, a blast, blight .

urina.definition: ūrīna ae, f urine, C., Iu.

urinator.definition: ūrīnātor ōris, m urinor, a diver , L.

urinor.definition: ūrīnor —, —, ārī, dep. urina, to plunge under water, dive : qui urinantur, divers .

urna.definition: urna ae, f 1 VAS-, a vessel of baked clay, vessel for drawing water, water-pot, water-jar, urn : fictilis, O.: stetit urna Sicca, H.: Caelata (of a river-god), V.— A voting-urn, ballot-box : senatorum: leges minitatur…

urnula.definition: urnula ae, f dim. urna, a little urn, waterpitcher : fictiles urnulae.

uro.definition: ūrō ūssī, ūstus, ere VAS-, to burn : nocturna in lumina cedrum, V.: picem, O.— To burn up, destroy by fire, waste by burning, reduce to ashes, consume : hominem mortuum: agros, L.: arces, H.: urenda filix, H.: cum fro…

ursa.definition: ursa ae, f ursus, a bear, she-bear : Catulus, partu quem reddidit ursa, O.—As a constellation, the Bear : Parrhasis, the Great Bear , O.: Erymanthis, the Little Bear , O.

ursus.definition: ursus ī, m a bear: circumgemit ursus ovile, H., O., Iu.: poscunt Aut ursum aut pugiles, i. e. a bear-baiting, H.

urtica.definition: ūrtīca ae, f VAS-, a nettle, stinging-nettle , H., Ct.—Fig., a spur, incentive, stimulant : divitis, Iu.— An itch, unhallowed desire , Iu.

uspiam.definition: ūspiam adv., at any place, anywhere, somewhere: sive est illa (lex) scripta uspiam, sive nusquam: si qua uspiam navicula apparuisset: utrum consistere uspiam velit, an, etc.

usquam.definition: ūsquam adv. —Of place, at any place, anywhere (usu. with a negat.): iste, cui nullus esset usquam consistendi locus, etc.: Numquam etiam fui usquam, quin, etc., T.: non usquam id quidem dicit omnino, he nowhere says p…

ustor.definition: ūstor ōris, m VAS-, a burner of the dead, corpse-burner .

ustulo.definition: ūstulō —, —, āre uro, to burn up, consume by fire : scripta ustulanda lignis, Ct.

usurpatio.definition: ūsūrpātiō ōnis, f usurpo, a taking into use, making use, using, employment, adoption, undertaking, use : usurpatio et renovatio doctrinae: vocis, L.: vetustatis.
